name: Proud Presenter
layout: Someone proudly presents an achievement in the caption; the picture behind them shows the disaster it caused.

name: Fixed It Dialogue
layout: 3-4 panels: problem raised, "Done.", "How?", the absurd method. Punchline is the last short line.

name: Expectation vs Reality
layout: 2 panels: the brochure, plan or promise; then the same thing in real life.

name: Job Ad vs The Job
layout: 2 panels: the job advert line over a glossy scene; the actual first day over the real scene.

name: How It Started / How It's Going
layout: 2 panels, same place and people: the hopeful start, then the same scene months later.

name: Day 1 vs Day 400
layout: 2 panels: the same employee on day 1 and on day 400; lines are what they say to a newcomer.

name: Escalation Ladder
layout: 3-4 panels: management's 'solutions' to one problem, each more absurd than the last.

name: Handover Note
layout: Caption is the note left for the next shift; the picture shows what the next shift actually finds.

name: Official Notice
layout: Caption is a real-sounding policy or sign; the picture shows staff following it literally, with absurd results.

name: Two Sides of the Counter
layout: 2 panels of the same moment: what the customer sees, then what is happening behind the counter.

name: Nobody / Management
layout: 2 panels: "Nobody:" over a calm scene; then the manager doing the unrequested, absurd thing.

name: POV
layout: Caption starts with "POV:" and puts the reader in the worker's shoes; the picture is that first-person view.

name: Silent Reaction
layout: 2-3 panels of setup; the last panel is only a face (line is "...") that lands the joke.

name: Meeting Agenda
layout: 3-4 panels, each one agenda item read aloud; the last item reveals the absurd priority.

name: Five Stages
layout: 4 panels: one worker's denial, anger, bargaining and 'acceptance' of a new policy; acceptance is absurd.

name: Training Video vs Shift
layout: 2 panels: the cheerful training video's line; the real shift doing the same task.

name: Boss Quote, Staff Face
layout: Caption is a short quote from the boss; the picture is only the staff's reaction, which is the punchline.

name: Tiny Detail
layout: An ordinary, calm work scene; one small detail in the picture is the joke, and the caption points at it innocently.

name: Outsider Solves It
layout: 2-3 panels: experts stuck on a problem; a customer, child or cleaner solves it in one line.

name: Clock Time-Lapse
layout: 3-4 panels labeled by time (9:00, 9:05, 9:06): a calm start that collapses fast.

name: Ticket Status
layout: Caption is an official status update ("Resolved", "On schedule"); the picture shows the reality.

name: Customer Review
layout: Caption is a cheerful 5-star review; the picture reveals what the customer did not notice.

name: Specialist Vision
layout: 2 panels: what a normal person sees in a place; what someone from this profession sees in the same place.

name: Distracted Boyfriend
layout: Template: a man turns from his partner (the old duty) toward a passer-by (the shiny new thing).

name: Two Buttons
layout: Template: a sweating person chooses between two buttons; both choices are bad, or the wrong one wins.

name: Drake
layout: Template: rejecting the sensible option (top), approving the absurd one (bottom).

name: Crying Cat Interview
layout: Template: an outsider reads a bad sign as a great sign.

name: Roll Safe
layout: Template: a person taps their temple; the caption is a 'clever' idea that defeats the purpose.

name: This Is Fine
layout: Template: a calm figure with coffee in a room on fire, saying everything is fine.

name: Grave Selfie
layout: Template: a smiling person poses at the grave of something staff lost.

name: Moe Throws Barney Out
layout: Template: a problem is thrown out, then is back at the bar in the next frame.

name: Baboon and Sleeping Lion
layout: Template: someone creeps up on a calm, sleeping target, holding the thing that will wreck it.

name: Fish Bait
layout: Template: a fish bites the same labeled bait again.

name: Soldier Shields the Wrong Side
layout: Template: a soldier heroically shields one side while the attack comes from the other.

name: The Plan
layout: Template: four whiteboard steps of a plan; in step 4 the presenter realizes the plan backfires on them.

name: Expanding Brain
layout: Template: 3-4 rising levels of 'enlightenment', each idea worse than the last.

name: Bike Fall
layout: Template: a cyclist jams a stick into their own wheel, then blames something else on the ground.

name: Is This a Pigeon
layout: Template: someone confidently mislabels an obvious thing.

name: Monkey Looks Away
layout: Template: an awkward glance away when someone asks the uncomfortable question.

name: Clown Makeup
layout: Template: 4 steps of believing the same promise again, ending in full clown makeup.

name: Then vs Now
layout: Template: a strong, capable 'then' beside a feeble 'now', about the same job or team.

name: Trade Offer
layout: Template: 'I receive: ... You receive: ...' with a lopsided deal from management.
